title: Mayhem in Monsterland
build: Apex disk release, the contributor's own G64 images of both sides; sha256 of each in orientation.md

records.c: The 6510's memory configuration port: boot runs with the value it finds (it never writes $01); $36 (KERNAL in, BASIC out) from `2` ($C241) and the intro's set-up ($52EE); $35 briefly at $8099, then $36 again from the raster set-up $8390 (A = $36 at $8238 and $8BB8); $36 in the game loader ($5401), $34 for the copier, $35 handed to the engine.

False symbol: $A9 is the operand of the BIT zero page that the music driver's file copy has at $4CEA (run $0526). The intro patches it into BIT absolute ($2C at $535A), so BIT $00A9 does read $A9, but only for flags that the LDA at $4C16 overwrites after the return; the patch's point is that the bytes $A9 $00 after the $2C are LDA #$00 (run $0527), the target of the BNE at $4CE0. No other instruction reads $A9.

KERNAL's current secondary address; the game loader sets $60 (open channel 0 for reading) before $F3D5 opens the file.
KERNAL's current device number (8), read by both loaders for TALK and LISTEN.

High byte of mus_ptr ($00FC).

Bottom of the stack page. boot fills $0100-$01FF with $02 so that LOAD's RTS returns to $0203, and at $0249-$024B writes $C2 here: the high byte JMP ($01FF) picks up, the page-wrap of the indirect jump.
Run-time address of the copier (loaded at $5700, put here by $53D0-$53D9, 49 bytes). The game loader jumps here when `game` is in.
Run-time address of the copier's source high byte (operand of LDA $A800,Y), decremented page by page from $A8 to $5A.
Run-time address of the copier's destination high byte (operand of STA $FF00,Y), decremented from $FF to $B1.
Top byte of the stack page: boot stores $40 here, the low byte of JMP ($01FF) ($C240 once the page wraps to $0100).
First byte of `game` at run time: the game loader's load pointer starts here (STA $0200 at $54C9).

Side 1's autostart, `boot`, loaded over the stack page by the KERNAL's LOAD: $0100-$01FF are all $02, so the RTS that ends LOAD pops $0202 and resumes here. Blacks the border and background, clears $9D (no KERNAL messages), points the NMI vector $0318/$0319 at $0227 (an RTI) and starts CIA 2's timer A with its NMI enabled, so the NMI line stays held and RESTORE does nothing. Then resets the stack, SETLFS 1,8,1, writes the file name "2" ($32) at $3232 and names it there (SETNAM, length 1, X/Y = $32/$32), LOADs `2` to $C000 and jumps to $C240 through JMP ($01FF): $01FF holds $40 and the 6502 takes the high byte from $0100 (= $C2), not $0200.

records.s: $80 $40 is the undocumented two-byte NOP #$40 here; its second byte, $0227, is the RTI the NMI vector points at
the file name is the one byte A = $32 ("2"), stored at $3232 so that X = Y = $32 name it
indirect jump across a page edge: low byte from $01FF ($40), high byte from $0100 ($C2), so it lands on $C240

Music driver, loaded at $4B00-$52FF and copied by $533C-$5358 to $033C-$0B3B, where it runs (subtract $47C4 from an address here for its run address; jumps and tables inside name run addresses). This byte (run $033C) is the driver's on switch: cleared by the init ($0810) and the stop ($0591), incremented to 1 when init has primed the tune ($058B); the per-frame entry $0879 does nothing while it is 0.

Run at $033D, called by mus_update every frame. One step of the three-voice player: counts the frame divider $0959 up to the tempo $0958 (a tick when it wraps to 0); adds the filter sweep step ($0975 fine, $0976 coarse) to the cutoff in $0A1B/$0A1C; then for each voice X = 2..0 (Y = its SID register offset, 0/7/14, from $09FC): steps the arpeggio counter, and on a tick, only when the voice's note is on its last tick ($09F3 = 1 with $09A8 = 0) or $09A8 = $FF ($4B66-$4B79), reads the voice's command events (two bytes each: command + 1, argument) and dispatches each through the 37-entry handler table at $0A1F/$0A44 by patching the JSR at $03D5; then, unless the note is a rest ($0960 = 0), runs the per-frame effects (slide $076B, vibrato $06A6, waveform programme $096C, arpeggio $0677, pulse sweep $0621); and on a tick counts the note down ($0462). It reaches the SID only through the shadow at $0A06-$0A1E.

records.s: run $036C: top of the voice loop, X = voice 2, 1, 0
run $03B7: command loop; an event byte below $26 is a command (byte - 1 indexes the handler table), anything else ends the run of commands
run $03D5: JSR whose operand ($03D6/$03D7) is written from the handler table just before; A = the event's second byte, Y = the voice's register offset

records.c: Run at $0462. Counts the voice's note length down by one tick (16 bits: $09F3 low, $09A8 high); releases the gate (clears bit 0 of the control shadow) once the remainder drops below the release point $0966; at zero falls into mus_next_note.

Run at $0488 (entered from $0462 when a note runs out). Clears the voice's effect counters, resets the filter sweep if this is the filter voice ($0957), loads attack/decay ($09CC), sustain/release ($09C3) and pulse width high ($09C9) into the shadow, then reads the next note event: byte 1 is the note (0 = rest, bit 7 ignored), turned into a frequency through mus_note_freq with the arpeggio partners ($0996, $0993) worked out too; byte 2 is the length in ticks; the waveform $09C6 goes to the control register with the gate on. A following event $19 gives the length a high byte ($09A8).

records.s: run $0526: BIT. In the file this byte is $24 (BIT zero page), which would leave the $00 at $0528 to run as BRK on this path; $535A-$5363 patch it to $2C (BIT absolute) so it skips the LDA #$00 and stores the pulled length byte

records.c: Run at $052D (the init $080A ends here). Clears the driver's variables $0957-$09F1, sets each voice's release point to 2, length to 1 tick and vibrato speed to 1, the tempo $0958 to 1; keeps the tune's address in $09FF/$0A00 and sets the voices' event pointers: voice 0 at tune + 4, voices 1 and 2 at tune + 4 plus the 16-bit offsets in the tune's first four bytes. Silences the shadow (mus_silence), runs two ticks to prime it, and switches the driver on ($033C).
Run at $058F. Switches the driver off ($033C = 0) and falls into mus_silence.
Run at $0594. Clears the SID shadow $0A06-$0A1D and writes 0 to the SID volume register $D418.
Run at $05A2, command $0F. A = repeat count: counts the voice's loop counter $09D2 up and, while below A, moves the event pointer back to the loop start saved by command $10 ($09D8/$09DE).
Run at $05BE, command $10. Saves the voice's event pointer as the loop start ($09D8/$09DE) and clears the loop counter $09D2.
Run at $05D0, command $11. As command $0F but with the voice's second loop slot (index X + 3), so loops can nest two deep.
Run at $05D8, command $12. As command $10 with the second loop slot (X + 3).
Run at $05DE, command $13. Sets the voice's transpose $09BA (semitones added to every note).
Run at $05E2, command $04. A of 100 or more sets the release point $0966 (A - 100 ticks before the end of a note); below 100 sets how many ticks the waveform programme runs ($096F).

Run at $05F0, command $06. A of 99 or more chooses the filter voice $0957 (A - 100), whose notes restart the filter sweep; below 99 selects the voice's waveform programme $096C: 1-5 put a waveform from $0A01-$0A05 on the voice from the note's second tick until $096F ticks (the whole note when $096F = 0); 6 and up alternate waveform (programme - 5) with the note's own on every other arpeggio step (bit 0 of $09A2).
Run at $05FE, command $14. Splits A into the voice's pulse-sweep limits: high nibble to $09B4, low nibble to $09B7.
Run at $060D, command $15. Sets the voice's vibrato period $09F0 (frames per quarter swing).
Run at $0611, command $16. Sets the shadow of $D417 ($0A1D): filter resonance and which voices go through the filter.
Run at $0615, command $17. Sets $0977, the cutoff the filter voice's notes restart the sweep from.
Run at $0619, command $1A. Adds A to the shadow of $D418 ($0A1E): volume and filter mode.

Run at $0621, called every frame for a voice whose sweep rate $09CF is non-zero; acts only on frames where the arpeggio counter $099F is 0. Moves the voice's 16-bit pulse width ($0A08/$0A09 in the shadow) up or down by the rate, reversing against the limits $09B4 and $09B7 ($09B1 holds the direction).
Run at $0673, command $02. Sets the voice's waveform/control byte $09C6, written to the SID with the gate on at each note.

Run at $0677, every frame for a voice with arpeggio mode $0969 set. Mode 1 alternates the frequency between the note and the second note ($097B/$097E) on odd ticks of $09A2; other modes cycle three frequencies (note, $097B/$097E, $0999/$099C) by the step $0990.

Run at $06A6, every frame for a voice with vibrato depth $0987. After the delay $098A runs out, adds or subtracts the depth to the frequency ($095A/$095D) by quarter of the cycle $09AE, each quarter $09F0 frames long.
Run at $06DE, command $1B. Sets $0996, the interval of the arpeggio's third note above the played note.
Run at $06E2, command $1C. Sets the filter sweep step: A / 8 to $0976 (coarse), A AND 7 to $0975 (fine).
Run at $06F0, command $24. Sets the tempo $0958: frames per tick.

Run at $06F4, command $1E. Sets $0993, the interval of the arpeggio's second note. Its RTS at $06F7 is also command $18, which does nothing: the byte $19 that selects it is read by the note code as a length high byte ($0516).
Run at $06F8, command $19. Adds A to the voice's transpose $09BA.
Run at $0700, command $20. Sets the vibrato delay $098D (frames after each note start).
Run at $0704, command $23. Returns from a call (command $22): takes the saved event pointer from $09E4/$09EA, moves the older one down from $09E7/$09ED, and steps past the call.
Run at $071D, command $1F. Sets the voice's detune $09A5, added to the low byte of every note frequency.
Run at $0721. Adds the vibrato depth $0987 to the voice's frequency $095A/$095D and to the shadow.
Run at $0736. Subtracts the vibrato depth $0987 from the voice's frequency and writes the shadow.
Run at $074F. A = note (bit 7 dropped) plus the voice's transpose: looks up the frequency in the note table at $0A69 and adds the detune $09A5; returns low byte in A, high byte in Y.
Run at $0767, command $0B. Sets $09C0, the high byte of the slide speed.

Run at $076B, every frame once the slide delay $0981 has passed. Mode $0978: 1 slides toward the target frequency $097B/$097E and stops there, 2 slides up, 3 slides down, by the 16-bit speed $09BD/$09C0.
Run at $07C7. Adds the slide speed $09BD/$09C0 to the frequency $095A/$095D and writes the shadow.
Run at $07DA. Subtracts the slide speed from the frequency and writes the shadow.
Run at $07ED. Copies the voice's frequency $095A/$095D into the SID shadow ($0A06/$0A07 + Y).
Run at $07FA, command $0D. Sets the pulse-sweep rate $09CF (0 = no sweep).
Run at $07FE. Advances the event pointer $FC/$FD by two bytes; returns Z clear (the command loop's BNE uses it).

Run at $080A: the driver's entry for a new tune, A/X = the tune's address (low/high). Switches the driver off and continues at $052D (mus_init_tune). Called with $9EB6 for the Mayhem TV and Apex part ($5386) and $9A00 for the roll call ($53BF).
Run at $0816, command $08. Sets $0981, the ticks after a note's start before the slide begins.
Run at $081A, command $0A. Sets the vibrato depth $0987 (0 = none).
Run at $081E, command $0E. Sets the slide mode $0978 (0 off, 1 to target, 2 up, 3 down).
Run at $0822, command $07. Sets the arpeggio mode $0969.
Run at $0826, command $05. Sets $0972, frames per arpeggio step.
Run at $082A, command $01. Sets $09CC, the attack/decay byte written at each note.
Run at $082E, command $00. Sets the shadow of $D418 ($0A1E): filter mode and master volume.

The intro's entry, jumped to by `2` when `menu` is in. Reached from the Mayhem TV and Apex part through JMP $800A when its last fade ends ($8BD2). Blacks the background and turns on extended colour and multicolour together ($D011 bit 6, $D016 bit 4), a combination the VIC shows as black, so the screen stays dark; waits about half a second in two delay loops (256 x 256 and 150 x 256 rounds), starts tune $9A00 (the roll-call music) and jumps to $80D6.

The intro's exit, reached through JMP $8007 when fire is pressed during the roll call ($827B-$8282). Masks interrupts and writes 0 to the SID's volume register $D418 25 times (the loop's store is not indexed, so it never reaches the other 24 registers; the volume alone silences the music), copies the copier $5700-$5730 to $0180-$01B0 and jumps to the game loader at $C000 (the copy of $5400). The game is loaded only now, with the screen blanked by the loader.

OPEN 15,8,15 with the one-character name at $53FF ("I"), then CLOSE 15 and CLRCHN: sends the drive the Initialize command after `2`'s drive program, so the drive is back in its normal state before the next load.

The loader for `game`, at its load address: $5321-$533A copies $5400-$57FF to $C000-$C3FF and $53DB jumps to $C000 once fire is pressed, so every address inside it is a $C0xx/$C1xx run address. Sets $01 = $36, masks the VIC interrupts, silences the SID, blanks the screen and turns the sprites off; opens "GAME" ($53DE) on device 8 with the KERNAL's serial routines, writes the drive program at $C168 (= $5568 here) into drive RAM $0700 with M-W in 32-byte pieces, starts it with M-E $07AB, builds its 2-bit decode table at $C400-$C4FF from the 32 seeds at $C134 (= $5534), then receives `game` through $C0FF into $0200 upwards until the page counter reaches $A9 ($0200-$A8FF), changing the border colour every block. Then calls UNLSN ($EDFE, at $54E4; not UNTALK), closes the file (LISTEN, secondary $E0, UNLISTEN) and jumps to the copier at $0180.

records.c: Run at $C0FF. Receives one byte from the drive program over CIA 2 port A ($DD00): raises the handshake, waits for bit 7, reads four bit-pairs at fixed cycle spacing and combines them through the decode table at $C400/$C408/$C410/$C418. Returns it in A and changes the border colour (EOR with the operand at $C112, stepped once per block).
The game loader's receive routine continues here (run address $C100): the handshake's second half and the four bit-pair reads.
Run at $C134: the same 32 seed bytes as `2`'s at $C362, from which $54A6 builds the receive decode table at $C400-$C4FF.
Run at $C154. Sends LISTEN to the current device ($BA), secondary $6F (the command channel), then "M-"; the caller adds "W" or "E" and the rest of the drive command.

records.c: Draws a credits page for page $8011: turns the sprites off, blacks both background zones ($82DF, $82FE), clears the text and landscape areas to char $FF ($8433) and their colour to black ($846D), resets the three bar sets to dark ($8881), waits until the background reads black (the raster is in a black zone), then prints the upper small-font line ($94A4) at $4568, the big-font name ($9082) at $45B8 and the lower small-font line ($94AE) at $4630, and moves to the next page.

Roll call's main loop. Restores the KERNAL exit of the raster interrupt ($84B8), starts the raster chain at $8288 ($01 = $36; raster_install sets the first interrupt at line $F9) and then once a frame: waits for frame_flag; on next_page draws the next dinosaur page; counts the show timer ($8A6C); on draw_credits draws the credits page; checks for Mayhem's page ($8A93); toggles the frame parities; and when fire is pressed on joystick port 2 ($DC00 bit 4 low) leaves through exit_hook ($8007).

Raster handler at the bottom of the picture (line $CA, $DA or $DF; line $F9 the first time, from raster_install). Blacks the background, sets frame_flag, scrolls the mountains ($852A), steps the landscape and sprite colour fades ($8AC2, $8ADE), on Mayhem's page runs his run-in, stop, skid and dust ($8740-$87CA), once the dinosaur has arrived scrolls the name and Latin name in ($8B2E, $8B5C), plays the music ($8003); returns the next link: the credits chain at line 0 ($833E), the title bars at line $51 ($832F, bar set 0), or the sky at line $6A ($82DE).

Raster handler at line $6A, the top of the landscape window: sets the sky colour (the LDA's operand at $82DF, per page), moves the dinosaur in ($86F9) unless it is Mayhem's page, animates its frames ($86A3) unless Mayhem has stopped, scrolls part of the ground ($85F5); next link line $A2 ($82FD).
Operand of LDA #: the sky colour for $D021 in the landscape window's top, written by $89C9 from the page's colour record and by the grey fade; 0 on a credits page.

Raster handler at line $A2: sets the lower zone's background colour (operand at $82FE), scrolls the nearest ground strips ($85C6) and the clouds ($84EC); next link the Latin name's bars at line $D1 ($8320, bar set 1) once the title bars are on, else the bottom handler at line $CA.
Operand of LDA #: the background colour from line $A2 down, written by $89C3 from the page's colour record and by the grey fade; 0 on a credits page.
Raster handler at line $D1: draws the colour bars behind the Latin name (row 20), then black; next link line $DF ($8288).
Raster handler at line $51: draws the colour bars behind the big-font name (rows 4-5, bar set 0, rainbow), then black; next link line $6A ($82DE).
Credits chain, line 0: selects the bar set for the upper small-font line (operand at $833F); next link line $79 ($834A).
Operand of LDX #: the bar set of the credits page's two small-font lines, 11 (black) to 7 (full), written by the fades from $9607/$9610 and by $8881.
Credits chain, line $79: bars behind the upper small-font line, then black; selects the big name's bar set (operand at $8353); next link line $89.
Operand of LDX #: the bar set behind the credits page's big-font name, 6 (black) to 2 (full), written by the fades from $95F5/$95FE and by $8881.
Credits chain, line $89: bars behind the big-font name, black, then selects the lower line's bar set (operand at $8367); next link line $A1.
Operand of LDX #: the bar set of the credits page's lower small-font line, written together with $833F.

Credits chain, line $A1: bars behind the lower small-font line, black, then runs the credits timeline: wait ($87E7), fade in ($87FD), hold ($8826), fade out ($8843), wait and ask for the next page ($886C); next link line $DA ($8288).

Starts a raster-interrupt chain: A = value for $01, X/Y = the first handler (kept in the JSR operand $83FD/$83FE). Turns off the CIA interrupts and acknowledges them; with carry set on entry uses $83E9 as the interrupt entry, with carry clear $83EF (both callers clear it); writes the entry to both $0314/$0315 (KERNAL vector) and $FFFE/$FFFF (the RAM vector used when the KERNAL is switched out); sets the exit to $EA7E; enables the raster interrupt at line $F9 and stops CIA 1's timer A, then CLI.

records.s: X/Y = the interrupt entry chosen by the carry

records.c: Low byte of the value $83C0 writes into the exit jump's operand ($8409), $7E; $84A7 would change it to $B2 and $84B8 sets it back.
The value $83C5 writes into the exit jump's high byte ($840A), $EA; $84A7 would change it to $84.

Interrupt entry for the hardware vector $FFFE (KERNAL switched out): clears carry and pushes A, X and Y as the KERNAL would, then continues at $83EF. Chosen by raster_install when called with carry set, which no caller does.

Interrupt entry (through $0314): acknowledges a raster interrupt, calls the current handler through the patched JSR ($83FD/$83FE), and takes the handler's answer as the next link: A = raster line ($D012), X/Y = the next handler. Leaves through the patched JMP at $8408 ($EA7E, the KERNAL's register restore and RTI).
Low byte of the current raster handler (operand of the JSR at $83FC), set by raster_install and after each handler from X.
High byte of the current raster handler, from Y.
Low byte of the interrupt's exit jump, $7E ($EA7E), or $B2 after $84A7.
High byte of the interrupt's exit jump, $EA, or $84 after $84A7.

Fills the screen $4400-$47E8 with the character in X and colour RAM $D800-$DBE8 with the colour in A (both held as operands, $8422 and $8414), in four interleaved 251-byte runs. $8B7D uses char $E7 and black, $80EC char $FF and black.
Operand of the LDA # in fill_screen: the colour stored in colour RAM, written from A at $840E.
Operand of the LDA # in fill_screen: the character stored on the screen, written from X at $840B.
Fills with char $FF the title rows 4 and 5 and the Latin row 20 (40 columns each) and the landscape window, rows 7-18, columns 6-33.
Sets colour RAM to 0 (black) over the same areas as clear_text_areas.
Unreached: nothing calls it. Would point the interrupt's exit at $84B2 (pull Y, X, A and RTI) instead of the KERNAL's $EA7E, as needed with the KERNAL switched out.
Unreached exit (see $84A7): pulls Y, X and A and returns from the interrupt.
Points the interrupt's exit at $EA7E, the KERNAL's restore and RTI. Run before each raster chain is started.

X = bar set 0-11: points the colour bars at its colour table ($9535/$9541 into $804C/$804D), sets its line count ($954D into $8060) and chooses the second store: $D020 (border too) if $9559 is non-zero, else the dummy $803A. All twelve sets use the dummy.

records.s: A/Y = high/low byte of the bars' second store target

records.c: While the landscape scrolls, every other frame: rolls the eight pixel rows of the 14-character strip $7D60-$7DCF (characters $AC-$B9, the clouds of rows 7 and 9) one pixel left, the bit leaving the left edge coming back at the right, so the cloud row repeats every 14 characters and drifts half a pixel a frame.

While the landscape scrolls, on the other frames: rolls two pixels left the 7-character strips of the mountains, $7DD0-$7E07, $7E08-$7E3F, $7E40-$7E77, $7E78-$7EAF and $7EB0-$7EE7 (characters $BA-$DC, rows 11-15): one pixel a frame on average, twice the clouds' speed.

While the landscape scrolls, every frame: rolls four pixels left the bottom two pixel rows of the 3-character ground strip at $7EEE ($DD-$DF, row 16) and the top four rows of the strip at $7F00 ($E0-$E2, row 17).

While the landscape scrolls, every frame: rolls two pixels left the top six rows of the ground strip at $7EE8 ($DD-$DF, row 16), and six pixels left the lower four rows of $7F04 ($E0-$E2) and the top five rows of $7F18 ($E3-$E5, row 18): with $85C6 the ground moves faster the nearer the bottom of the window it is.

Y = page. Takes the page's number of animated sprites from $9804 and, for each of sprites 4, 5 and (on three-sprite pages) 6, the next entry of the animation table at anim_index: its frame list's address ($97C2/$97D8) into the LDA operand at $86B6, $86D3 or $86EA, and its length - 1 ($97EE) into the slot's frame index and wrap value.

While the legs animate: writes each animated sprite's next frame from its frame list into its pointer ($47FC-$47FE), stepping its index down and wrapping. On a non-Mayhem page only on even frames; on Mayhem's page every frame.
Low byte of sprite 4's frame-list address (operand of LDA $FFFF,Y), set by anim_setup.
High byte of sprite 4's frame-list address.
Low byte of sprite 5's frame-list address.
High byte of sprite 5's frame-list address.
Low byte of sprite 6's frame-list address.
High byte of sprite 6's frame-list address.

After the walk delay ($800F): moves sprites 4, 5 and 6 (as many as the page animates) one pixel right a frame ($D008, $D00A, $D00C) and counts each one's steps; when a counter runs out the dinosaur has arrived ($8064).
Mayhem's page: after the walk delay, moves sprites 4 and 5 right two pixels a frame until sprite 4's X is $F8, then sets mayhem_stop and legs_frozen.
Mayhem's page, once: shows the standing frames $A9 and $AA in sprites 4 and 5, starts the skid (24 steps from $98AA) and the dust cloud (11 frames from $98C5).
Mayhem's page: moves sprites 4 and 5 left each frame by the next value of $98AC plus one (2 pixels at first, rising to 4; 70 pixels over 25 steps); after the last step he has arrived ($8064).
Mayhem's page, on even frames: shows the next dust-cloud frame ($98C7-$98D1) in sprite 6, placed $25 pixels left of sprite 4.
Credits timeline, on half the frames (half_parity 0): counts fade_in_wait down; at 0 starts the fade-in (8 steps, $9619).
Credits timeline: each step sets the bar sets of the big name ($8353, from $95F5) and of the two small lines ($8367 and $833F, from $9607); after the last starts the hold (140, $961C).
Credits timeline: counts the hold down; at 0 starts the fade-out (8 steps, $961A), except on page 10, the "press fire to continue" page, which stays up.
Credits timeline: steps the bar sets back to black from $95FE and $9610; after the last starts the wait before the next page (40, $961D).
Credits timeline: counts the last wait down; at 0 asks for the next dinosaur page (next_page).
Sets the credits page's bar sets to the black ones: 6 for the big name ($8353), 11 for the small lines ($8367, $833F).

Prints a small-font string to the screen or a buffer: A/X = destination (high/low, kept in the STA operand $88C8/$88C9), Y = string number, looked up in $908E/$90AC. Strings are screen codes ending in $FF; a space leaves the cell as it is, "1" and "2" print the brackets ($AA, $AB), every other code c prints character c + $8F (letters a-z are characters $90-$A9).
Low byte of the string address (operand of LDA $FFFF,Y), from $908E.
High byte of the string address, from $90AC.
Low byte of the destination (operand of STA $FFFF,Y), from X.
High byte of the destination, from A.
The five punctuation marks the big font has, as screen codes: "!", ".", ",", "?", ":"; a match at index i draws glyph $24 + i.
Width flag for each punctuation mark: 0 = one column, non-zero = two ("?" only).

Prints a big-font string, two rows high: A/X = destination (high/low, kept in $89A3/$89A4), Y = string number from $8EDE/$8EF2. Each character is a glyph of four characters from the map at $7500 (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right) written to the destination and 40 bytes below; a space advances one column; letters advance two columns except i, j, l (one column), and m and w, which get a third column (glyphs $29 and $2A); punctuation from $88CE; digits would index past the map (code + $2A). Strings end in $FF.
Low byte of the big-font string address (operand of LDA $FFFF,Y), from $8EDE.
High byte of the big-font string address, from $8EF2.

records.s: advance the destination by the column step held in $8983

records.c: Operand of the ADC # at $8982: how many columns the big-font character just drawn advances (1 or 2), written at $8907 and $8959.
Operand of the LDY # at $899B ($FF in the file): print_big saves its string index here at $88EC before Y is reused for the glyph stores, and reloads it at $899B.
Stores A at the big-font destination + Y (operand $89A3/$89A4) and advances Y.
Low byte of print_big's destination (operand of STA $FFFF,Y), advanced as characters are drawn.
High byte of print_big's destination.
print_big's state: $89A7 = 1 after an m (a third column follows, glyph $29), $FF after a w (glyph $2A), 0 otherwise; $89A8 is cleared with it and not read.
Cleared with $89A7 at the start of each big-font string ($88F4); nothing reads it.

Y = page: reads its four-byte colour record (pointer from $94B9/$94C3) and sets $D023, $D022 (the character multicolours) and the sky and ground background colours ($82FE, $82DF). The grey fade ($8AC2) enters at $89B3 with its own record in $7E/$7F.

records.s: entry of the fade: $7E/$7F = a four-byte colour record

records.c: Y = page: reads its 40-byte sprite record (pointer from $961E/$9628) from the end: the eight sprite pointers to $47F8-$47FF, the 16 position bytes to $D000-$D00F, the eight colours to $D027-$D02E, then $D026, $D025, $D015, $D017, $D01D, $D01C, $D010 and $D01B.
When the dinosaur arrives: sets colour RAM of rows 14, 15, 17 and 18 (columns 6-33) to 9, multicolour with white as the character's own colour, replacing the page's yellow or cyan in the grey scene.
A slide of 35 NOPs ending in RTS at $8A61; the colour bars call it at $8A56, eleven NOPs from the end, as a fixed delay. The first 24 NOPs are never run.
Entry into the NOP slide used by the colour bars: eleven NOPs and the RTS at $8A61, a fixed delay before the first bar line.
Clears the roll-call variables $8021-$803D and falls into show_timer_step.

Once the show timer is on: counts it down (on Mayhem's page only on even frames); at 0 switches to the credits page (credits_mode and draw_credits) and starts its timeline with the 30-step wait ($961B).
Once, when page 9 is reached: sets mayhem_page and mayhem_running and disarms itself ($8020).
Turns on multicolour text mode ($D016 bit 4).
Turns off multicolour text mode; nothing calls it.
RTS ending multicolour_off, also the exit grey_fade branches to ($8AC5, $8AD6) when it has nothing to do.

On odd frames while fade_step runs: takes the next four-byte colour record from $94FF/$9508 and applies it through $89B3 (sky, ground, $D022, $D023), records 8 down to 1, white first and ending with $9515 (light grey sky and ground, $D022 = $0C, $D023 = $0B); record 0 ($9512) is never applied.

On odd frames while sprite_fade_step runs: takes the next five-byte sprite colour record ($98D2/$98DB, or $9912/$991B on Mayhem's page) and sets the sprite multicolours $D025/$D026 and the colours of sprites 4, 5 and 6, with sprite 7 (the sun) white.

Once the dinosaur has arrived: scrolls title rows 4 and 5 one character left and puts the next column of the big-font name from the buffers $775C/$7784 at the right edge, until it meets the 0 end marker.

Once the dinosaur has arrived: scrolls row 20 one character right and puts the next character of the Latin name from the buffer $7734 (read from the end) at the left edge, until it meets the 0 marker at $7734.
Mayhem TV and Apex part: set to 1 by the raster handler $8C0A each frame; the loop at $8BBE waits for it and decrements it.

Mayhem TV and Apex part. Fills the screen with char $E7 in black ($840B), copies the two rows of "COMPUTER · PRODUCTIONS" from $76E4 and $770C to rows 12 and 13, puts four single characters at rows 11 and 14, columns 0 and 20 ($8A, $8E, $8B, $E6; their purpose is unknown), turns extended colour off, and starts its raster chain at $8BD8 ($01 = $36; first interrupt at line $F9). Then waits for each frame and toggles frame_parity until $8BCF has been changed to 1 ($8DBB), when it jumps to the roll call through $800A.
Operand of the LDA # at $8BCE: 0 in the file, so the BEQ after it loops; $8DBB writes 1 when the Apex screen has faded out, and the loop then falls through to JMP $800A.

Mayhem TV and Apex raster handler at line $59 (line $F9 the first time, from raster_install): blacks border and background and loads sprite set 0 (the APEX letters) once the logo has gone, else set 2 (the Mayhem TV logo); next link line $83.
Raster handler at line $83: once the logo has gone loads sprite set 1 (the white bar that wipes across "COMPUTER · PRODUCTIONS") for the lower half; next link line $B9.

Raster handler at line $B9: runs the APEX sequence (letters $8CF1, curtain $8C4D, curtain fade $8D6B, final fade $8D8F) or, before it, the Mayhem TV logo's fade ($8DBF); plays the music, sets tv_frame_flag; next link line $59.

records.s: music, frame flag and the next link

records.c: Mayhem TV and Apex state: $8C30 APEX letters animating (1 in the file), $8C31 curtain moving, $8C32 logo gone (0 = Mayhem TV logo still up), $8C33-$8C36 delays before letters A, P, E and X start ($1E, $05, $05, $0D frames, counted on odd frames), $8C37 delay before the curtain moves (40), $8C38 delay before the logo fades in and between its fade-in and fade-out (100, counted on even frames), $8C39 delay before the final fade (150), $8C3A curtain steps left (14).
APEX sequence: 1 while the wipe bar moves (curtain_move), set when the X has finished.
0 while the Mayhem TV logo is up; 1 once it has faded out, which switches the raster handlers to the APEX sequence.
Delay before the letter A starts zooming in, $1E (30) odd frames.
Delay before the letter P starts, 5 odd frames after A's.
Delay before the letter E starts, 5 more.
Delay before the letter X starts, $0D (13) more.
Delay before the wipe bar moves, 40 frames.
Delay before the Mayhem TV logo fades in and its hold at full white, 100 even frames each (reloaded at the $FF in $8EC3).
Delay before APEX and its text fade out, 150 odd frames.
Steps of the wipe bar's movement left, 14.

Sprite enable masks for the curtain set, applied from the end as the bar moves ($8C91, Y = $8C3A before its decrement, 14 down to 2): $03, $03, $07, $07 ... $FF, one more sprite every two steps, so the bar's blocks appear one by one behind its moving edge; 13 masks are applied, and the first two bytes ($8C3B, $8C3C) are never read.
$D010 bits flipped when the bar's sprites 0 ($8C4A = $01) and 1 ($8C4C = $02) cross X = 255; $8C4B ($FF) is not read.

APEX sequence, after the letters: after a 40-frame delay moves the bar's sprites 0 and 1 right 24 pixels a frame (flipping their $D010 bits on overflow) and steps the enable mask from $8C3B; after 14 steps colours rows 11-14 white ($8C98), puts the bar behind the text ($8E2D = $FF) and starts its colour fade ($8EB6).
Colours rows 11-14 of colour RAM white; entered at $8C9A with any colour in A (the final fade).
Colours rows 11-14 of colour RAM (the "COMPUTER · PRODUCTIONS" text and the single characters) with A.

Y = sprite set 0-2: copies its 36-byte record (pointer $8E03/$8E06 into $39/$3A) to the VIC from the end: pointers to $47F8-$47FF, positions to $D000-$D00F, colours to $D027-$D02E, then $D015, $D01D, $D010 and $D01B.

APEX sequence, on odd frames: for each of the four letters in turn, after its delay ($8C33-$8C36), steps its sprite pointer ($8E25-$8E28) back through its frame list ($8E79, $8E88, $8E97, $8EA6), from a dot growing to the full letter; when the X is complete stops and starts the curtain ($8C31).
APEX sequence, on even frames: sets all eight curtain sprite colours to the next value of $8EB7 (white, then greys to black, read from the end); after the last starts the final fade ($8ED4 = 8).

APEX sequence, after a delay of 150 odd frames, on odd frames: sets the text rows' colour and the four letters' colours ($8E0D-$8E10) to the next value of $8ED5 (white to black); after the last writes 1 to $8BCF, which ends the part.

Mayhem TV logo, on even frames: after the delay at $8C38 steps the colours of the logo's six sprites ($8E55-$8E5A) through $8EC3 from the end: grey to white, a 100-frame hold at the $FF, white to black; then hands over to the APEX sequence ($8C32, $8C30).

Addresses of the three 36-byte sprite sets of the Mayhem TV and Apex part, low bytes then high bytes: set 0 $8E09 (APEX letters), set 1 $8E2D (wipe bar), set 2 $8E51 (Mayhem TV logo); read by tv_load_set ($8CAC).
High bytes of the three Mayhem TV and Apex sprite-set addresses ($8E at $8E06-$8E08).

Sprite set 0, the APEX letters (36 bytes, read by tv_load_set from the end): $D01B 0, $D010 0, $D01D 0, $D015 $0F (sprites 0-3); colours (8) white for sprites 0-3; positions (16) X $7C, $9C, $BC, $DC at Y $6C; pointers (8) $61 (blank) for sprites 0-3, stepped by apex_letters through the zoom frames to the letters A ($AB), P ($B3), E ($BB) and X ($C3).
Colours of the APEX letters (sprites 0-3, $8E0D-$8E10), written by apex_fade_out as the letters fade to black.
Sprite 0's pointer in set 0: the letter A's current zoom frame, written by apex_letters from $8E7A-$8E87.
Sprite 1's pointer in set 0: the letter P's frame, from $8E89-$8E96.
Sprite 2's pointer in set 0: the letter E's frame, from $8E98-$8EA5.
Sprite 3's pointer in set 0: the letter X's frame, from $8EA7-$8EB4.
Sprite set 1, the white bar that wipes across under the APEX letters (36 bytes). This byte is its $D01B: 0 (in front of the text) until curtain_move sets $FF (behind it).
Set 1's $D010 ($82: sprites 1 and 7 past X = 255), with bits flipped by curtain_move as sprites 0 and 1 move right.
Set 1's $D01D: $FC, sprites 2-7 double width.
Set 1's $D015, the enable mask: $03 to start, then $8C3B's masks as the bar moves.
Set 1's eight sprite colours ($8E31-$8E38), white; curtain_fade steps them to black.

Set 1's positions ($8E39-$8E48): sprite 0 (the round edge) at X 0, sprite 1 at $E8 with its $D010 bit set (off the right edge), sprites 2-7 from $18 to $108 in steps of $30, all at Y $91; curtain_move adds 24 a frame to the X of sprites 0 and 1. Pointers follow at $8E49: $CD (the round edge) and $60 (a solid block) for the other seven.
Sprite set 2, the Mayhem TV logo (36 bytes): $D01B 0, $D010 0, $D01D 0, $D015 $3F (sprites 0-5).
Colour of logo sprite 0 ($8E55-$8E5A: sprites 0-5), all set together by tv_logo_fade.
Colour of logo sprite 1, set by tv_logo_fade.
Colour of logo sprite 2, set by tv_logo_fade.
Colour of logo sprite 3, set by tv_logo_fade.
Colour of logo sprite 4, set by tv_logo_fade.
Colour of logo sprite 5, set by tv_logo_fade. Then two unused colours, the positions ($8E5D: X $9A, $B2, $CA at Y $6C and $81) and the pointers $CE-$D3 at $8E6D.
Index into each APEX letter's frame list, $0E (14) to start, counted down by apex_letters.
Index into the letter P's frame list, from $0E.
Index into the letter E's frame list, from $0E.
Index into the letter X's frame list, from $0E.
Zoom frames of the letter A, read from the end: $CC, $CC, $CC, $CB, $CB (a dot), $B2 down to $AB (the A, growing), $FF at the start ends the list.
Zoom frames of the letter P, from the end: the dots $CC/$CB, then $BA down to $B3; $FF ends it.
Zoom frames of the letter E, from the end: dots, then $C2 down to $BB; $FF ends it.
Zoom frames of the letter X, from the end: dots, then $CA down to $C3; $FF ends it.
Length of the wipe bar's colour fade, $0A (10), copied to $8EB6 when the bar stops.
Step of the wipe bar's colour fade, 10 down to 0 (curtain_fade).
Colours of the wipe bar's fade, read from the end (index 10 to 1): white five times, light grey, light grey, grey, dark grey, black; the first byte is not read.
Step of the Mayhem TV logo's fade, $10 (16) down to 0 (tv_logo_fade).

Colours of the Mayhem TV logo, read from the end (index 16 to 1): black, dark grey, grey, light grey, white, then $FF (hold for 100 frames), light grey, grey, dark grey, black; the first byte is not read.
Step of the final fade of APEX and "COMPUTER · PRODUCTIONS", 0 until curtain_fade sets 8.
Colours of the final fade, read from the end (index 8 to 1): white, light grey, light grey, grey, grey, dark grey, dark grey, black; the first byte is not read.
Addresses of the 20 big-font strings ($8F06-$9081), low bytes then high bytes: 0-9 the dinosaur names, 10-19 the credits names.
High bytes of the 20 big-font string addresses ($8EF2-$8F05).
Big-font string 0: "stegosaurus" (5 leading spaces, $FF at the end), the name on dinosaur page 0; screen codes, drawn by print_big through the glyph map at $7500.
Big-font string 1: "megasaurus" (5 leading spaces, $FF at the end), the name on dinosaur page 1; screen codes, drawn by print_big through the glyph map at $7500.
Big-font string 2: "ballodactyl" (5 leading spaces, $FF at the end), the name on dinosaur page 2; screen codes, drawn by print_big through the glyph map at $7500.

Run-time address of the game loader's load pointer, the low byte of the STA operand at $54C9 (= $C0C9 run time), from $00. In the hand-over it is inside `2`'s leftover code.
Run-time address of the high byte of the game loader's load pointer, $02 to $A8; the load ends when it reaches $A9 ($54D4-$54D9). In the hand-over it is inside `2`'s leftover code.

`2`, side 1's fast loader, entered from boot. Sets $01 = $36, acknowledges and masks the VIC interrupts, silences the SID, blanks the screen and turns off the sprites. Opens "MENU" (name at $C396) through the KERNAL's serial routines, writes the 256-byte drive program at $C3A8 into drive memory $0700 in eight 32-byte M-W commands, starts it with M-E $07AB, builds the 256-byte 2-bit decode table at $0600 from the 32 bytes at $C362, then receives `menu` byte by byte through $C32D into $4B00 upwards until the page counter reaches $B0 ($4B00-$AFFF), flashing the border on every block, drains three more pages and jumps to the intro at $52ED.
Run-time address of $5700 in the game loader's copy (the copier's source). In the hand-over: the high byte of the JSR $C32D at $C2FE in `2`'s loader.

records.s: the store's operand is the load pointer, $4B00 in the file, stepped by $C304-$C30C; the snapshot shows the value it was left at

Receives one byte from the drive program over CIA 2 port A ($DD00): raises the handshake line, waits for the drive to answer on bit 7, then reads four bit-pairs at fixed cycle spacing, each read looked up in the decode table at $0600/$0608/$0610/$0618 and ORed together. Returns the byte in A. Also changes the border colour (EOR with the operand at $C340).

records.s: the EOR's operand ($C340) is stepped once per block by $C316, so the border colour changes on every block received

records.c: Operand of the EOR at $C33F: the value `2` flips the border colour with on every byte; stepped once per block by $C316, so the border flicker changes with every block loaded.
32 seed bytes from which $C2D6-$C2EA builds the receive decode table at $0600-$06FF (each byte repeated eight times); four groups of eight, one for each bit-pair position the receiver reads.
Sends LISTEN to the current device ($BA) with secondary address $6F (the command channel) and then the characters "M-"; the caller adds "W" or "E" and the rest of the drive command.
The file name "MENU" in PETSCII, 4 bytes, named by SETNAM at $C266-$C26C.

14 bytes after the file name that no code in `2` reads: as words they are $FFD2 followed by the KERNAL's default STOP, GETIN, CLALL, user-command, LOAD and SAVE vectors ($F6ED, $F13E, $F32F, $FE66, $F4A5, $F5ED), presumably whatever followed the name in memory when the file was saved.

1541 drive program, 256 bytes, sent to drive RAM $0700-$07FF by the M-W loop at $C283 and started at $07AB by M-E. It sets up the drive's timer, takes the file's first track and sector from $18/$19, and runs itself as a job (code $E0); it calls the drive ROM ($F50A, $F8E0) to read and decode each sector and sends every data byte to the C64 as four 2-bit pairs on the serial bus's CLOCK and DATA lines ($1800). The same 256 bytes are in the intro's game loader at $5568.

Run-time address of the game loader's 2-bit decode table, $C400-$C4FF, built by $54A6-$54B2 from the seeds at $5534 and read by its receive routine at $C11E-$C133. In the hand-over these bytes are the tail of `2`'s drive program (described at $C3A8).
Run-time address of the second eight-entry group of the game loader's decode table (bit-pair 2), read at $C124. Hand-over bytes: `2`'s drive program.
Run-time address of the third group of the game loader's decode table (bit-pair 3), read at $C12A. Hand-over bytes: `2`'s drive program.
Run-time address of the fourth group of the game loader's decode table (bit-pair 4), read at $C130. Hand-over bytes: `2`'s drive program.

In the hand-over: the last 80 bytes of `2`'s drive program ($C458-$C4A7, drive addresses $07B0-$07FF, including the entry $07AB just before). At run time: the end of the game loader's decode table ($C458-$C4FF).
The last 88 bytes of `2`, after the drive program: not reached by any code here and not read by the drive program; they look like fragments of 6502 code left in the file when it was saved.

KERNAL ROM at $EA7E (checked in kernal 901227-02): reads $DC0D to acknowledge CIA 1, pulls Y, X and A and returns from the interrupt. The intro's raster interrupt leaves through JMP $EA7E ($8408). The RAM underneath holds nothing of the intro.
KERNAL ROM TALK (the target of the $FFB4 jump-table entry): the loaders send TALK to the drive before reading. RAM underneath: not the intro's.
KERNAL ROM LISTEN (target of $FFB1): opens the drive's command channel for the M-W and M-E commands ($C382, $5554) and for the close. RAM underneath: not the intro's.
KERNAL ROM SECOND (target of $FF93): sends the secondary address after LISTEN ($6F for the command channel, $E0 to close). RAM underneath: not the intro's.
KERNAL ROM TKSA (target of $FF96): sends the secondary address after TALK. RAM underneath: not the intro's.
KERNAL ROM CIOUT (target of $FFA8): sends one byte to the listening drive; the loaders send the drive program and the "M-W"/"M-E" commands with it. RAM underneath: not the intro's.
KERNAL ROM UNLSN (target of $FFAE): ends a command to the drive. RAM underneath: not the intro's.
KERNAL ROM ACPTR (target of $FFA5): reads a byte from the talking drive; the loaders call it once after TALK, before switching to their own 2-bit transfer. RAM underneath: not the intro's.

Inside the KERNAL's OPEN, at $F3D5 (it starts by testing the secondary address $B9 and the name length $B7): the serial-device step that sends the file name set by SETNAM to the drive, which makes the drive find the file. Both loaders call it directly instead of OPEN. RAM underneath: not the intro's.

KERNAL SETLFS: logical file, device, secondary address (A, X, Y). RAM underneath: not the intro's.

KERNAL OPEN, through the vector at $031A; used by drive_initialize ($53F4). RAM underneath: not the intro's.
KERNAL CLOSE, through $031C; used by drive_initialize. RAM underneath: not the intro's.
